Try it at the table

Spider Webs

Gather your things, then try each one. Guess first. Then look closely and write or draw what you saw.

What you need

  • notebook
  • pencil
  • clipboard or stiff cardboard
  • optional magnifying glass
  • optional camera or phone zoom
  • soft morning light (outdoors)

TRY 1Which lines are sticky on an orb web?

  1. From a few steps away, sketch a web you can see.
  2. Mark the hub, three spokes, and one loop of the spiral.
  3. Do not touch the silk.

  1. On your sketch, label one spiral loop 'maybe glue' and write one question you still have about silk.

TRY 3How does a spider feel a tiny tug?

  1. Tap a table lightly with a pencil, then harder.
  2. Tell which tap felt bigger through your hand.
  3. That is only a toy model of vibration, not a real web.

TRY 4Why does dew make a web easy to see?

  1. On a cool morning, look for a web on a fence or bush.
  2. Count how many spiral loops you can see before the dew fades.
  3. Stay back and do not touch.
